Change an item's fields; --clear unsets those that can be unset

## Usage

```text
chainmail item update <id> [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
chainmail item update it_01jcb7m2k9r8q3v4w5x6y7z8a9 --state in-progress --due 2026-11-30
# drop the due date and the estimate
chainmail item update it_01jcb7m2k9r8q3v4w5x6y7z8a9 --clear due,estimate
```

## Flags

```text
      --area string               work or personal
      --clear strings             unset these, comma separated: area, priority, start, due, estimate, description
      --description string        the new description, as Markdown
      --description-file string   read the new description from this file
      --due string                the due date, YYYY-MM-DD
      --estimate float            the estimate
      --priority string           p0 to p3
      --start string              the start date, YYYY-MM-DD
      --state string              backlog, in-progress, in-review or done
      --title string              the new title
      --type string               the new type, which must fit the parent and every child
```

## Global flags

```text
      --output string   output format: json or table (default $CHAINMAIL_OUTPUT, then cli.toml, then table on a terminal, json otherwise)
      --socket string   daemon socket (default $CHAINMAIL_SOCKET, then cli.toml, then /run/chainmail/chainmail.sock)
```
